items.name: DRIVE_BIAS_MAX
items.doc: The bias at `character = +1`, in the SHAPER's own input units — `OMX_DRIVE_BIAS_MAX`. DERIVED, not chosen. In the saturating limit every knee tends to `sgn`, the output is a rectangular wave of duty `d = ½ + asin(b)/π`, and its `n`th harmonic goes as `sin(nπd)/n` — so `|H2|` is maximal at `d = ¾`, which is `b = sin(π/4) = 1/√2` exactly. Measured too: the H2-maximising bias for a full-scale sine at unity drive is 0.712 (soft), 0.658 (tape), 0.645 (tube), and this one value costs 0.000 / 0.035 / 0.088 dB of H2 against each curve's own optimum. ONE normalised bias for all three knees, not three.

items.name: DRIVE_AMOUNT_RANGE
items.doc: The PRE-CURVE gain, in dB. 0 dB is unity into the curve, so a stage switched on at its defaults changes almost nothing — which is what an `on` switch should mean. The ceiling is where every curve is saturating hard on any signal a console carries.

items.name: DRIVE_CHARACTER_RANGE
items.doc: The EVEN/ODD harmonic balance. −1 is pure odd (the curve itself), +1 is pure even, 0 an equal blend — the kernel splits its own distortion residue into an odd and an even half and fades between them, so the two ends are exact rather than approximate (`mix_drive.h`, measured: H2 at −317 dBc at −1, H3 at −118 dBc at +1). Unitless, and signed by construction. NOT NORMALIZED_RANGE: this is a BALANCE with a meaningful centre, and a 0..1 travel would put its centre at 0.5 and its neutral nowhere.

items.name: DRIVE_BAND_FREQ_RANGE
items.doc: The band split / tilt corner, in Hz. ONE travel for all three band modes, because the C imposes one constraint on all of them: it is the corner of a single biquad, and the split's other half is `x − LP(x)`. The full audio band, not the channel filters' narrower HPF/LPF pair — the same reasoning REVERB_CUT_RANGE records: a surface narrower than the row removes reach the console genuinely has.

items.name: DRIVE_MIX_RANGE
items.doc: The wet/dry, as a PERCENT — the unit a drive control is read in on every desk that has one. Deliberately not NORMALIZED_RANGE (which is unitless 0..1): a mix a surface must label "0.35" when the operator thinks in "35 %" is a control whose declaration is fighting its reader. The kernel divides by 100 where it resolves the atom, in one place. The come-up is 100 %, not the reverb's modest 30: a saturator's insert use is IN the path. The `exciter` curve seeds itself lower (DRIVE_EXCITER_SEED), because that is a property of the TOPOLOGY and not of the travel.

items.name: DRIVE_TRIM_RANGE
items.doc: The POST-stage make-up, in dB. Symmetric enough either way that an operator can null the stage in and out against the bypass, which is how a colour stage is actually judged.

items.name: DRIVE_CURVES

source.origin: omx-dsp 6d6fcda include/omxdsp/fx/omx_drive.h enum omx_drive_curve; the console engine's drive curve list

items.doc: The drive's shaper curves, in the order of the integer the kernel reads. Exciter runs the soft shape in a parallel-sum topology.

items.name: DRIVE_BANDS

source.origin: omx-dsp 6d6fcda include/omxdsp/fx/omx_drive.h enum omx_drive_band; the console engine's drive band list

items.doc: Which part of the spectrum the drive's curve is fed, in the order of the integer the kernel reads. The split is complementary, so mix 0 stays bit-identical to the dry signal.

items.name: DRIVE_AUTO_GAINS

source.origin: omx-dsp a624f26 include/omxdsp/fx/omx_drive.h:138 struct omx_drive.auto_gain, omx_drive_instance.h:166 (on); the console engine's drive state defaults auto gain to on

items.doc: The drive's AUTO-GAIN switch: on, the stage measures its own level change and matches it out (`omx_drive.h`'s `struct omx_drive.auto_gain`), so turning the drive up adds colour rather than loudness. A field of the console's drive row (`DriveState.autoGain`), on at come-up there and in omx-dsp's drive face.

items.name: DRIVE_STEREO_LINKS

source.origin: omx-dsp a624f26 include/omxdsp/fx/omx_drive.h:139 struct omx_drive.stereo_link, omx_drive_instance.h:167 (on); the console engine's drive state defaults stereo link to on

items.doc: The drive's STEREO LINK switch: on, ONE auto-gain path is driven by both legs' summed energy, so the image cannot shift under the level match; off, each leg matches its own (`omx_drive.h`'s `struct omx_drive.stereo_link`). A field of the console's drive row (`DriveState.stereoLink`), on at come-up there and in omx-dsp's drive face.

items.name: DRIVE_HF_ROLLOFFS

source.origin: omx-dsp a624f26 include/omxdsp/fx/omx_drive.h:140 struct omx_drive.hf_on, omx_drive_instance.h:168 (off); the console engine's drive HF roll-off choices (off, 12000, 16000), defaulting to off; each id carries its corner in Hz, off none (operator ruling, 2026-10-13)

items.doc: The drive's post-curve HIGH-FREQUENCY ROLL-OFF: `off` (the section does not run: `omx_drive.h`'s `struct omx_drive.hf_on` is 0), `12000` or `16000`, each carrying its corner in Hz as its value and `off` none (operator ruling, 2026-10-13: the choice is an enumeration and the frequency is data of each member, so no 0 Hz doubles as a sentinel). The ids are the console's drive-row wire vocabulary (`DriveState.hfRolloff`, what the drive row's OPTIONS publishes and a session stores), so the console re-exports this set; a kernel reads the corner from the id's value. It comes up off, as omx-dsp's drive face does.

items.name: DRIVE_OVERSAMPLES

source.origin: omx-dsp 483818c include/omxdsp/fx/omx_drive.h:105-109 omx_drive_factor_of (1, 2, 4), omx_drive_instance.h:81 OMX_DRIVE_INSTANCE_FACTOR (OMX_OVS_MAX_FACTOR, omx_oversampler.h:135: 4); the console engine's drive oversampling factors (1, 2, 4), defaulting to 4

items.doc: The drive's OVERSAMPLING factor: the shaper runs inside the console's one oversampler at 1x, 2x or 4x, and the id is the factor (`omx_drive.h`'s `omx_drive_factor_of` member set, `struct omx_drive.os_factor`). A field of the console's drive row (`DriveState.oversample`, the console's DRIVE_OVERSAMPLE_FACTORS; the set is named for its control), 4 at come-up there and in omx-dsp's drive face (OMX_DRIVE_INSTANCE_FACTOR, the oversampler's largest).
